inline_comments.body: **RAVF001 [high] data semantics** — This adds a second mapping for the same CSVs. It uses different score units, metric IDs, versions, evaluation IDs, and source metadata.

inline_comments.body: **RAVF002 [medium] remote input** — The current V2 CSV contains `NullModel`, and this loop writes it as a normal model.

inline_comments.body: **RAVF003 [medium] error handling** — Handled fetch or write failures print an error and `Done!`, then the module exits with status 0.
inline_comments.source_kind: untouched historical finding from a requested PR

inline_comments.body:
**RAV-RUN1-R1-F001 [medium] filesystem traversal** — `os.walk` ignores scan errors when `onerror` is unset. A readable file can still validate after an unreadable subtree is skipped.

An `os.walk` error callback can stop partial scans and name the inaccessible path. A mocked scan error can test this without platform-specific permission behavior.
inline_comments.source_kind: untouched historical finding from a requested PR

inline_comments.body:
**RAV-RUN1-R1-F001 [medium] API contract** — The docstring calls `output_dir` a collection directory, but supported callers also pass report-identity paths such as `data/lm_eval_samples`.

The parameter can be described as a path below the nearest `data` root. Its relative components form the report name; `data/<collection>` is the usual adapter case.
inline_comments.source_kind: untouched historical finding from a requested PR

inline_comments.body:
**RAV-RUN1-R1-F002 [medium] report placement** — The nearest ancestor named `data` controls placement. A nested `data` component can leave `adapter_reports` inside an outer datastore tree.

The docs can state that the nearest `data` ancestor wins. A repeated-`data` example makes the placement limit concrete.
inline_comments.source_kind: untouched historical finding from a requested PR
